claims.text: tron: the inference program under test. kv_cache.hpp is its KV cache store; the public interface is the book and page structs.

fields.definition: The inference program under test. kv_cache.hpp is its KV cache store, whose public interface is the public methods of the book and page structs.

claims.text: slot (logical slot, kv_slot_id): one KV cache storage unit that one or more attention operations write and read; storage is reclaimed by slot, not by layer.

fields.definition: One K/V storage unit of the book, selected by kv_slot_id. Several attention operations can consume one slot. A page holds one kv_block per (slot, KV head).

claims.text: storage slot (kv_storage_offset): an absolute slot offset in the book's physical allocation, as opposed to a logical slot seen through the active view.

fields.definition: An absolute K/V slot offset in a book's physical allocation. It selects storage, not a logical slot of the active view. The EAGLE storage is the extra physical slot at kv_storage_offset(logical_slot_count()).

claims.text: EAGLE / EAGLE storage view: a speculative-decoding mode with an extra physical KV slot; while set_storage_view selects it, logical slot zero addresses that extra slot.

fields.definition: The book's secondary view for EAGLE (a speculation model). While it is selected (set_storage_view), logical slot zero addresses the extra physical slot. The K layout state keeps one extra entry (layout_t::n_slots) for that storage.

claims.text: KV head: one key/value head of the attention geometry; kv_geometry is {n_kv_heads, head_size}; a page has one kv_block per (slot, KV head).

fields.definition: One key/value head. kv_geometry holds n_kv_heads and head_size. One kv_block is the KV cache for one KV head in one KV slot of one page.

claims.text: plane: the K (or V) data of one KV head of one page, 64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16 = 16 KiB.

fields.definition: K for one KV head of one page: 64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16, 16 KiB, the same bytes in the row-major and the VNNI layout.

claims.text: panel: one (dimension step, token block) tile of the VNNI plane, 16 pair rows of 64 bytes = 1 KiB, exactly one AMX B tile; a plane has 16 panels.

fields.definition: One 1 KiB tile of the VNNI plane for one 32-dimension step and one 16-token block: 16 dimension-pair rows of 64 bytes. A panel is exactly one AMX B tile.

claims.text: pair row: one 64-byte line of a panel holding one dimension pair (two consecutive dimensions, 4 bytes) for 16 consecutive tokens.

fields.definition: One 64-byte line = 32 bf16 = 16 dwords: the two values of one dimension pair for each of 16 consecutive tokens.

claims.text: VNNI: Vector Neural Network Instructions; the VNNI layout stores the two values of a dimension pair of one token next to each other, the B-operand layout of the AMX tile multiply and of the AVX-512 pair dot product.

fields.definition: Vector Neural Network Instructions. In the VNNI layout the two values of a dimension pair of one token are stored side by side; one 64-byte row holds that pair for 16 tokens. It is the B-operand layout of the AMX tile multiply (TDPBF16PS) and of the AVX-512 pair dot product (VDPBF16PS).

claims.text: AMX: Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, the CPU's tile instruction set; the AMX QK kernel reads the VNNI plane in place as its B operand.

fields.definition: Advanced Matrix Extensions, the tile instruction set of the CPU. The AMX QK kernel qk_vnni_128x4 reads a page's VNNI plane in place as its B operand (the second matrix of the tile multiply).

claims.text: AVX-512: the CPU's 512-bit vector instruction set; k_vnni::qk_group is the AVX-512 reader of VNNI K with one token per vector lane.

fields.definition: Advanced Vector Extensions, the CPU's 512-bit vector instruction set. The software reader of VNNI K (k_vnni::qk_group) is AVX-512 code with one token per lane.

claims.text: bf16: the 16-bit brain floating-point format of the stored K and V values; fp32 is the 32-bit float the scores are accumulated in.

fields.definition: bf16 is the 16-bit brain floating-point format of the stored K and V values. fp32 (32-bit float) is the accumulation format of the score kernels; the two readers' fp32 add order differs.

claims.text: GOF: group of four consecutive tokens whose K/V rows the staging copies into a buffer that DMA moves to the FPGA card.

fields.definition: Group-of-four: 4 tokens of KV data (one k_hwcacheblock and one v_hwcacheblock of 8 KB each) that the staging (gof::populate) copies into a buffer and DMA transfers to the card.

claims.text: staging: the copy of a GOF's K and V rows from the pages into the hardware buffer through the page_info callbacks k_head_fn / v_head_fn.

fields.definition: The gather of one GOF's K/V rows from the pages into the hardware block buffer. page_info::k_head_fn(slot, kv_head, scratch) returns a pointer to the token's K row, in place for a row-major block or rebuilt in the caller's scratch for a converted block.

claims.text: DMA: direct memory access; the KV books live in DMA memory whose allocation creates the kv_block objects, which is why k_storage must stay trivially constructible.

fields.definition: Direct memory access. The KV books are DMA memory; the allocation itself creates the kv_block objects (Note [KV block lifetime]), so kv_block's members must be trivial to construct and destroy.

claims.text: HBM: High Bandwidth Memory, the FPGA device memory that holds the K/V of every DMA-complete GOF once a sequence has passed the engagement point.

fields.definition: High Bandwidth Memory, the FPGA device memory. The staging bytes and the HBM layout are unchanged by this PR.

claims.text: hardware attention (FPGA attention): the FPGA scores the K/V of DMA-complete GOFs; whether an operation uses it is decided once per model (cached_operation_uses_hw).

fields.definition: Attention scored by the FPGA (field-programmable gate array) over the K/V it holds. cached_operation_uses_hw(operation) says, once per model, whether an operation's K is scored there; then save_k records no row bits and the blocks stay row-major.
fields.source: model.hpp:1531-1533, Note [Row-major blocks under hardware attention] (kv_cache.hpp:729-764)

claims.text: main helpers: the helper threads of the main thread in generated plugins (TRON_MIN/MAX_MAIN_HELPERS); they are idle while main runs save_k, so a shared block save gives them work units.

fields.definition: Helper threads of the main thread in the generated plugins (count from TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS / TRON_MAX_MAIN_HELPERS). The generated run_main_help calls save_k with the helper's worker_ix so they share the K store.

claims.text: attention workers: the threads that run the attention jobs; each has its own Q/O channel; a pending page is read by them only after every minibatch that writes it counted its latch down.

fields.definition: The threads that consume Q and produce O for the attention jobs, one channel reader and writer per worker. They read a pending page only after every minibatch that writes it counted its latch down.

claims.text: tree lock (tree_lock): the global lock of the token tree; clear_kv_complete_at and copy_from run with it held, between forward passes, so no reader runs meanwhile.

fields.definition: The global tree_lock of the scheduler's token tree. The in-place transposes of k_forget_row (clear_kv_complete_at) and copy_from rely on it: no forward pass reads the book while it is held.

claims.text: acquire / release / acq_rel / relaxed: the C++ std::memory_order values on the atomic bit words; a release store or fetch_or publishes the plane writes before it, an acquire load sees them.

fields.definition: C++ std::memory_order values on the atomic words k_rows_saved_ and k_vnni_blocks_. A release fetch_or (block bit) publishes the plane writes made before it; an acquire load (k_block_is_vnni, k_vnni_blocks) sees them. relaxed carries no ordering (the move constructor).

claims.text: fetch_or / fetch_and: atomic read-modify-write that sets (or clears) bits in one word and returns the old value; note_k_row_saved uses fetch_or only when the row bit is clear.

fields.definition: Atomic read-modify-write operations: fetch_or sets bits and fetch_and clears bits in one word, returning the previous value. They are the locked instructions k_forget_row's fast path avoids.

claims.text: kill switch (TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1): the environment variable that disables the AMX kernels at run time; with VNNI K it keeps the layout and runs the AVX-512 VNNI reader, not the row-major dotter.

fields.definition: TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 in the environment disables the AMX attention kernels at run time. A TRON_K_VNNI binary then scores VNNI blocks with k_vnni::qk_group; it is an AMX-off run of the same layout, not a rollback to the row-major numerics.

claims.text: dense AMX path: the whole-page AMX scoring in self_attention.hpp, taken only when the query is packed, is_dense_amx_page holds, and (third gate) every block of the page is VNNI (k_vnni_blocks == BLOCKS_PER_PAGE_MASK_0XF).

fields.definition: apply_dense_amx_page: one AMX kernel call for a whole 64-token page. Gates: amx_q_packed != nullptr, is_dense_amx_page (every token relevant through one visible range), and k_layout_dense (page::k_vnni_blocks returns all 4 block bits). Otherwise the page takes the software loop.

claims.text: work unit and window: in a shared block save, main cuts the minibatch's items into work units (runs of consecutive items inside one 16-token block of one page); a window is one shared save_k of a (layer, pass) that main opens and the helpers join.

fields.definition: batch::k_store_window is the K store window of one minibatch, one per (layer, pass): main opens it in save_k, the main helpers join it. Work unit u = items[unit_start[u], unit_start[u + 1]), never crossing a page, a 16-token block, or a change of token_jobs_do_kv; threads claim units with fetch_add on next_unit.

claims.text: 16-token block (block c): the 16 page offsets 16 c .. 16 c + 15 of a plane, the unit of the layout transition; a 64-token page has 4 blocks (TOKEN_BLOCKS_4).

fields.definition: Page offsets 16 c .. 16 c + 15 of a plane, 4 KiB. A block holds row-major rows until all 16 rows are saved and it is converted in place; bit c of k_vnni_blocks_ records the conversion. k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16 = 16, TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 = 4.

claims.text: row-major tail block: a block whose 16 rows are not all saved; it keeps each token's 256-byte row contiguous inside the block's own 4 panels, so a row-major block and a VNNI block occupy the same 4 KiB.

fields.definition: A 16-token block that holds its rows row-major (token t owns 256 contiguous bytes at row_major_row) until all 16 rows are saved and block_to_vnni transposes it in place. Under hardware attention a block may stay row-major for good.
fields.source: Note [Row-major tail block] (tensor_k_vnni.hpp:437-456), Note [Row-major blocks under hardware attention] (kv_cache.hpp:729-764)

claims.text: k_rows_saved_ and k_vnni_blocks_: the page's K layout state, one 64-bit saved-row word and one 8-bit converted-block byte per storage slot, with one extra entry for the EAGLE storage.

fields.definition: std::array of std::atomic<uint64_t> (one bit per page offset) and of std::atomic<uint8_t> (one bit per 16-token block), each with layout_t::n_slots + EAGLE_STORAGE_SLOTS_1 entries. A set block bit implies the block's 16 row bits.

claims.text: state entry (k_state_ix): the index into the two bit arrays for a logical slot: layout_t::n_slots for slot 0 while the EAGLE view is active, the slot's own index otherwise.

fields.definition: The index of a slot's K layout state in k_rows_saved_ and k_vnni_blocks_. k_state_ix(slot) returns layout_t::n_slots (the EAGLE entry) for slot 0 while book.eagle_view_active(), else slot.i.

claims.text: k_storage_ref: the pair {kv_storage_offset offset, size_t state_ix} that names a physical storage slot together with its state entry; the block conversion and the page copy take it as one argument.

fields.definition: A struct of a physical storage offset and the index of its K layout state. k_storage_of(slot) builds it from a logical slot under the current view; copy_from builds it from the physical slot; save_k's pending list keeps it so a view change cannot redirect the conversion.

claims.text: forward end: the point after the plugin's run() joined its workers and wait_for_coop_gof drained the cooperative GOF staging, where convert_pending_k_blocks runs because no reader of the pass is left.

fields.definition: The end of one forward pass on the main thread, after run() joined the workers and wait_for_coop_gof returned. convert_pending_k_blocks converts the queued blocks there, the first point where no reader of this pass is left.

claims.text: uniform geometry / primary geometry: layout_t::uniform_geometry means every slot has the same kv_geometry; layout_t::primary_geometry is that geometry, also used for the EAGLE storage.

fields.definition: layout_t::uniform_geometry is true when every slot shares one kv_geometry; layout_t::primary_geometry is that geometry. The uniform-geometry overloads of set_k_row / get_k_row / note_k_row_saved forward to it, and the EAGLE storage uses it.

claims.text: page offset: a token's position 0..63 inside its page (offset_in_page); it decides the token's column in the VNNI plane, which is why a partial page copy moves token by token.

fields.definition: A token's position inside its 64-token page. In the VNNI plane the offset decides the token's block (offset / 16) and column (offset % 16), so copying a token to a different offset moves its bytes.

claims.text: kv_saves_: the existing per-token, per-slot save counter of a page (0 = neither K nor V saved, 1 = one saved, 2 = both); clear_kv_complete_at zeroes it before calling k_forget_row.

fields.definition: std::array indexed [offset][slot] of std::atomic<uint8_t>: 0 = neither K nor V saved, 1 = one saved, 2 = both saved. The K layout bits are a separate record beside it.
